A number on a ruler is not enough. Show where the measurement goes wrong.

2. Try the controls when your teacher gives you a turn. Point to the start and the end.

## Make a mark someone can use.

Your job: mark 8 3/8 inches from one starting edge. Practise here, then do it for real.

1. Choose paper or teacher-provided scrap at least 10 inches long. Name it: for example, “my paper strip.”
2. Place zero at its left edge. Keep the ruler straight. Find 8 inches, then move 3/8 inch farther: six 1/16 spaces or three 1/8 spaces.
3. Make a thin pencil mark. Lift the tool, reset zero at the same edge, and check the mark once.
4. Below, draw your piece and mark. Label the starting edge and the measured distance in inches. Save one record.

**Working on your own:** No physical ruler? Set the screen mark to 8 3/8 inches and check it. Draw that setup below and label it “screen practice.” This is practice evidence, not a claim that you used a real tool. On a sixteenths ruler, 3/8 = 6/16. Find two whole-inch marks and count the spaces between them to identify the divisions. A simple rectangle and a mark are enough. Your written number gives the size; your drawing does not need to be to scale.

## Would you give it the go-ahead?

Swap pieces. Check the mark before anyone relies on it.

1. Swap practice pieces with a partner. If you are alone, lift your ruler and check your own piece again.
2. Put zero at the same starting edge. Read the distance to the mark yourself. The required length is 8 3/8 inches.
3. Choose Ready if your reading matches the required mark. Otherwise choose Needs a fix and say exactly what should change.
4. Tell your partner first. Save your check below, then submit the three responses.

**Working on your own:** No partner? Recheck your own mark after resetting the ruler. Select “My own mark, measured again.” No tool or piece? Check the supplied example above and select that source. Its mark reads 8 5/8 inches; the required length is 8 3/8 inches. Decide what needs to change. “Move the mark back 1/4 inch” is useful feedback. “It is wrong” does not tell someone how to fix it.

blocks.markdown:
## Case B - Route the drain through the service zone

This is a dry classroom coordination model, not an installation approval or permission to alter framing. Original horizontal run is 18 ft; available service-zone depth is 8 in. Required slope is at least 1/4 in/ft. Pipe OD is 2 3/8 in. Minimum top and bottom clearances are 3/4 in each. All vertical dimensions use the zone top as datum. Two changes may be proposed for review: shorten the run to 16 ft, or deepen the zone to 8 1/2 in while keeping the 18-ft run. Other fittings, access and connections are not specified.

| Condition | Value |
|---|---|
| Original horizontal run | 18 ft |
| Available zone depth | 8 in |
| Required slope | 1/4 in/ft minimum |
| Pipe outside diameter | 2 3/8 in |
| Top / bottom clearance | 3/4 in each |
| Alternative 1 | 16-ft run; 8-in zone |
| Alternative 2 | 18-ft run; 8 1/2-in zone |

1. List fixed requirements and the two changes available for review.
2. Calculate original fall, required depth and quantified conflict. Reject an unsupported slope reduction.
3. Evaluate both alternatives, including remaining depth margin.
4. Draw a plan and longitudinal section for your proposed route: flow, horizontal run, slope, datum, elevations and outside envelope.
5. Write an RFI explaining what another trade must confirm before the proposal could be used.
